title: Another Hand Is Beckoning Us
description: Another Hand Is Beckoning Us in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: John Greenleaf Whittier wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 404, “Not Lost, But Gone Before”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: An-oth-er hand is beck-oning us, An-oth-er call is given; And glows once more with an-gel steps The path that leads to heaven.

lines: And glows once more with angel steps
The path that leads to heaven.
O, half we deemed she needed not
To give to heaven a shining one,
That He whose love exceedeth ours
Fold her, O Father, in thine arms,
Still let her mild rebukings stand
And her dear memory serve to make

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: John Greenleaf Whittier died in 1892.
credits: Words by John Greenleaf Whittier (1807–1892), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
